title: SHE LOOKED… THEN REACHED.
paragraphs: SHE LOOKED… THEN REACHED.
Brother, sister… listen closely.

Because Genesis 3 didn’t begin with rebellion.
It began with a look.

A quiet moment.
A curious thought.
A small reach of the hand.
And history broke.
The Moment That Changed Everything
The serpent didn’t start with force.
He started with a question.
“Did God really say…?” — Book of Genesis 3:1
That question planted a seed.
Eve looked again at the fruit.
The Bible slows down here, almost like a camera zooming in:

“When the woman saw that the fruit of the tree was good for food and pleasing to the eye, and also desirable for gaining wisdom…”
— Book of Genesis 3:6
Three temptations collided:

• Good for food — appetite
• Pleasing to the eye — attraction
• Desirable for wisdom — pride
Then it happened.
She reached.

Not a war.
Not a thunderstorm.
Just a hand moving toward a fruit.
And sin entered the human story.
The Pattern Is Still Alive
Temptation rarely shouts.
It whispers.

You look.
You linger.
You justify.
Then you reach.

A message you shouldn't answer.
A shortcut you know is wrong.
A compromise nobody else will see.
One small decision.
One reach.
And suddenly life changes direction.
But the Story Didn’t End in the Garden
Right there—inside the wreckage—God spoke a promise.
A prophecy buried in the judgment.

“He will crush your head.”
— Book of Genesis 3:15
Many theologians call this the Protoevangelium—the first whisper of the Gospel.
One day a Seed of the woman would come.
Jesus.

Where Adam failed, Christ obeyed.
Where Eve reached for the fruit, Jesus reached for the cross.
Through His death and resurrection, the curse that began in Eden is being undone.

From shame to redemption.
From hiding to forgiveness.
That’s the Gospel.
Let Me Ask You Something
What small decision changed your whole life?

The relationship you started.
The sin you entertained.
The moment you ignored God’s voice.
Or maybe…
The day you finally reached for Jesus instead of the fruit.

Because the same God who walked into Eden calling,
“Where are you?”
Is still calling today.
And His grace is stronger than your worst reach.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
